turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Hi! How are you doing these days?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What actually makes a villain good? Some are amazing and some are just boring.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: The best ones usually believe they're right. Their goal makes some kind of sense, even if their methods are awful.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: So not evil just for fun.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Exactly. When you can almost see their point, they become scary. A cartoon baddie who only wants chaos is harder to care about.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I loved that barely did anything.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Presence matters too. A calm, quiet villain who appears in a few scenes can feel more threatening than one who's shouting all the time.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Less is often more. If the hero talks about them before they ever show up, the tension builds on its own.
